sentence: This project studies how a fat tissue protein that moves triglycerides affects obesity, liver fat and atherosclerosis in mice.
This project builds computer methods that compare many mammal genomes to find what makes cancer more or less likely, then applies this to human cancers.
This project studies how living mammalian cells respond to broken DNA, using CRISPR tools and fluorescence microscopy to watch repair happen.
This project tries to find out how early life stress affects immune and epigenetic systems in the body and raises the risk of adolescent psychopathology.
This project builds a computer framework using deep learning to map how cells in individual tissue samples communicate with each other.
This project tries to find out what drives lung adenocarcinoma to develop and progress, a lung cancer linked to tobacco smoke.
This project tests whether a lysate made from mature megakaryocytes and platelets grown from fat cells can replace common supplements for growing stem cells.
This project studies how blood-forming stem cells with DNA mutations expand as people age and which diseases are linked to faster expansion.
This project tries to find out how certain Rac proteins help lung adenocarcinoma cells move and spread, using animal models.
This project studies how two histone methyltransferases shape the cells that form cartilage in the developing face and skull.
This project tries to find out how cancer cells overcome a limit on their lifespan so that it can be targeted.
This project studies how damage to small blood vessels in the brain leads to dementia, by sequencing the nuclei of human brain vessel cells.
This project studies how memory B cells and their antibodies differ across human tissues and ages, including responses to influenza and tetanus.
This project tests whether a computer program that screens medical chart data can help spot physical abuse in infants earlier.
This project provides molecular services such as sequencing and single-cell experiments that help cancer scientists test their research ideas.
This project uses bacterial genomic methods to study where bacteria that infect spine surgery wounds come from and how the microbiome of the back matters.
This project provides tests that measure how much HIV is in plasma and in cells, to support research on HIV and its cure.
This project provides mouse models and virus libraries so that gene programs in coronary artery disease and pulmonary arterial hypertension can be mapped with Perturb-seq.
